description: Qualification record for the Claude Code-native delivery integration's two layers: the trusted model-external binding that applies and attests the grant, workspace, fence, and run-pinned projection BEFORE admission, and the in-session projection that reads checkpoints, consumes immutable context, and submits normalized results AFTER it. Live legs were driven against a real authenticated Claude Code session by the qualification harness, never by the product. Product-owned properties are proven by in-process sensors named here. Nothing is claimed beyond what ran.

host.admissionSurface: session-scoped --settings composed by the binding (grant-derived permission allow rules, model-external PreToolUse interceptor, SessionEnd lifecycle hook) with --setting-sources set to the empty selection, so every ambient scope is excluded and the binding's digest-bound settings file is the session's only settings source

terminationProvenance.crashProvenance: structurally unavailable in V1 — no supported host supplies it, no daemon exists to observe it, and the vocabulary carries no discriminator for it, so no record can claim one
terminationProvenance.tierVerdict: Tier 2. Tier 1 mutation floor and Tier 2 graceful lifecycle events are live-probed on this host version. Tier 3 is REFUSED: a detached background child survived a clean session end in both the admission spike and this unit's own live lane, so descendant teardown is unverified, same-workspace resume stays gated, and operator-authorized takeover into a fresh worktree remains the designed — not degraded — resume path.
terminationProvenance.grammarEnforcement: the honesty rule lives in the frozen payload grammar, not in a caller: an unverified descendant teardown may only ever carry fresh-worktree-only resume, so a journal entry cannot record a Tier 3 claim this host does not support
terminationProvenance.entrypoint: the trusted host-runtime lifecycle integration only — the SessionEnd hook the binding wires, and the facade operation it drives. No model-callable tool can reach it, and the operation is absent from the CLI's session-facing command surface.
terminationProvenance.gradeSource: the graded capability record carried inside the pinned generation (qualifications/host-admission-capabilities.json), keyed on host id and exact host version. The facade operation takes no teardown parameter, the binding state file carries no teardown field, and every doubt — unreadable record, ungraded version, tier below 3, or a capability entry that is not `supported` — resolves to `unverified`, which can only narrow resume eligibility. The record is inside the pinned generation's digest closure, which the canonical recheck verifies before the read, so a session cannot edit it without fencing the delivery into security_blocked first.

liveProbes.question: is a tool invocation denied while no attestation is applied?

verification.surface: claude -p (v2.1.97) with the binding-composed --settings and --setting-sources set to the empty selection
verification.method: the session was asked to Write a file; the interceptor state carried no attestation; the file was checked on disk, not inferred from model output

liveProbes.question: does the identical invocation succeed once the grant is attested?
liveProbes.answer: yes — the side effect landed on disk

verification.surface: claude -p (v2.1.97), same prompt and settings, attestation present
verification.method: the control for the denial above: the same request under an attestation bound to the binding's current expectation produced the file, so the denial is attributable to the interceptor and not to an unrelated failure

liveProbes.question: can a candidate-planted .claude/settings.json widen the attested grant?
liveProbes.answer: no — the planted rule was inert under the binding's admission flags

verification.surface: claude -p (v2.1.97) in a directory carrying a planted .claude/settings.json allowing Bash and Write, admitted with an attested grant allowing only Read
verification.method: the attested grant contains NO tool that can create a file, so any side effect is attributable to the planted file alone; the session was asked to create a file by whichever tool worked, and the file was checked on disk and was absent. An earlier form of this probe granted Write and asked for Bash, which the session could satisfy with the granted tool — the live lane caught that and it was corrected before this finding was recorded.

liveProbes.question: does the SessionEnd lifecycle hook fire on a clean non-interactive end?
liveProbes.answer: yes — the marker is present after the clean exit

verification.surface: claude -p (v2.1.97) with a SessionEnd hook writing a marker file
verification.method: marker file present after the session exited cleanly

liveProbes.question: does a detached background child survive a clean host end?
liveProbes.answer: yes — the child was still alive after the clean end, so teardown is UNVERIFIED and the host stays below Tier 3

verification.surface: claude -p (v2.1.97) whose Bash tool detached a nohup child recording its pid
verification.method: child pid recorded by the session; liveness checked after the clean host end (kill -0 succeeded); the probe then reaped its own child

liveLane.excludedFromCheck: the lane drives a real authenticated host session and is never part of npm run check
liveLane.userConfigurationUntouched: the lane admits every session with --setting-sources set to the empty selection, so no ambient setting scope — user, project, or local — is read, and the binding wrote nothing outside its disposable directory. It does NOT isolate the host's own state: the session authenticates with, and writes its project history and transcripts into, the operator's real Claude Code configuration directory, exactly as any session that operator runs does.
liveLane.settingsComposition: the lane writes its settings file in the binding's shape and with the binding's admission flags rather than calling composeClaudeCodeSession, which requires a materialized projection the probe deliberately does not have; the flags are asserted identical by the host module's own suite.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: attestation binds host version, delivery, fence, trust epoch, grant digest, workspace, and projection digest; stale or sibling attestations open nothing
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: live: an unattested invocation produced no side effect and the attested control did; fixture: the conformance contract's stale-fence and sibling-delivery cases deny on both the Claude Code binding and the fake host

acceptanceCriteria.statement: discovery-configuration rendering is digest-bound, binding-exclusive, worktree-scoped, and torn down with the worktree; the consumption marker is injected at materialization and read back from fence-bound submissions
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: the digest is computed by one definition used at application and at every recheck; a mutated byte fails closed; a host write into the worktree's own project scope moves neither digest; teardown leaves no residue and does not disturb a sibling worktree; the marker binds delivery and fence and a submission against another run's projection is refused — defense in depth over the receipt digest on binding-owned files, not an independent proof against an uncompromised receipt

acceptanceCriteria.statement: host-specific delegation stays non-normative; normalized checkpoint outcomes are the compatibility target
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: one frozen conformance contract is satisfied identically by the Claude Code binding driving a real worktree and by an in-memory fake host, and a deliberately non-conforming host is caught rather than normalized away

notExercisedLive: the durable journal half of the SessionEnd path — the lifecycle hook firing was live-probed, and the records it writes are proven in-process by the scenario sensor

native subagent delegation inside a qualified session — the product neither supervises nor observes it by design; what is proven is that the product launches no agent process and manages no host agents or workspaces
same-workspace resume — unreachable on this host version by construction, and exercised only through a host graded with verified descendant teardown in the fixture leg
knownLimitations: The delivery journal is not defended against a granted shell capability on this host. The graded record claims commonGitAuthorityPathProtected for Codex's OS sandbox and deliberately does NOT claim it for Claude Code: the interceptor extracts write paths only for the file-writing tools, so a Bash invocation's filesystem writes are capability-gated but not path-gated. A session holding Bash can therefore append a journal entry directly, and the payload grammar only enforces a record's internal consistency. Closing this belongs to the host's own permission system, not to this integration.

A superseded session is closed by two locks — its fence-scoped binding state is voided at rebind, and its own admitted fence is baked into its hook command — but both live in files a granted shell capability can reach, for the same reason. They defend against superseded-session CONFUSION, which is what the resume path needs; they are not a boundary against a shell-capable session.
